purpose: Runtime adapter. Fashion direction must NOT be frozen into the Avatar Skill. This file is a SCHEMA; the instance is generated at task time from the current canonical catalogue so the skill stays identity-stable while the store's fashion direction evolves.

onStale: emit a wardrobeWarning naming the generation date

instanceShape.catalogueSource: path + SHA-256 of the build the context was derived from
instanceShape.activeCategories: list of category keys with live products
instanceShape.assortment: per-category list of {id, brand, name, category, subcategory, priceEUR, campaign, isNew, newUntil, tags}. isNew and newUntil are the RAW catalogue values, kept for provenance; they are not the freshness verdict
instanceShape.activeCampaigns: campaign keys present in the catalogue
instanceShape.newIn: product ids that are NEW as of asOfDate, decided by the canonical storefront rule — NOT the raw isNew flag
instanceShape.silhouetteVocabulary: derived from product names/tags — the shapes actually stocked
instanceShape.asOfDate: ISO-8601 date the freshness rule was evaluated against (--as-of, default today)
instanceShape.newInPolicy: human-readable statement of the freshness rule the instance was built with

rule: If no instance exists for this task, wardrobeSource=NONE and wardrobeConfidence=LOW. Never substitute avatar-source clothing.

freshnessRule.rule: A parseable newUntil decides freshness outright and is INCLUSIVE through 23:59:59 local time on that date. Raw isNew is only the fallback when newUntil is absent, empty or unparseable.
freshnessRule.whyItMatters: Raw isNew can stay true after a product's newUntil has passed. Reading it directly would hand the avatar skill a NEW IN set the Mall no longer shows, so the context would style from products the customer sees as ordinary stock.
freshnessRule.oneRule: The storefront and the fashion context must never carry two definitions of NEW. If isProductNew() changes, is_product_new() in build_fashion_context.py changes with it.
